Traditional Speculaas Biscuits

Served at: St. Nicholas Day

Makes about 3 dozen biscuitsPrep 30 min (plus 2 hours chilling)Cook 12-15 min

Speculaas biscuits are crisp, spiced shortcrust cookies deeply rooted in Dutch and Belgian traditions, especially around St. Nicholas Day (Sinterklaas). Their distinctive flavor comes from a blend of warm spices, and they are often pressed into beautiful wooden molds depicting scenes or figures related to the holiday, making them a festive and delicious treat for children and adults alike.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/4 cups (270 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/8 teaspoon ground cardamom
  • Pinch of white pepper
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 cup (226 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 3/4 cup (150 g) packed light brown sugar
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) milk
  • Optional: Whole blanched almonds for decoration

Method

  1. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, ginger, cardamom, white pepper, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
  2. In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, cream together the softened butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes.
  3. Gradually add the dry ingredient mixture to the butter mixture, mixing on low speed until just combined and a crumbly dough forms.
  4. Add the milk, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until the dough comes together. Be careful not to overmix.
  5. Divide the dough in half, flatten each half into a disk, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight. Chilling is crucial for flavor development and easier handling.
  6. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
  7. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one disk of chilled dough to about 1/8-inch (3 mm) thickness. If using speculaas molds, press the dough firmly into the floured mold, then carefully tap it out. If using cookie cutters, cut out desired shapes.
  8. Carefully transfer the cut biscuits to the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) between them. If desired, press a blanched almond into the center of each biscuit.
  9. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the biscuits are firm. They will crisp up further as they cool.
  10. Let the biscuits cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

Tips

  • For an even richer flavor, prepare the dough a day or two in advance and let it chill in the refrigerator; the spices will meld beautifully.
  • If you don't have speculaas molds, any decorative cookie cutters will work perfectly. You can also simply cut the dough into rectangles.
  • Store cooled speculaas biscuits in an airtight container at room temperature for up to two weeks, or freeze for longer storage.
